DIAGNOSIS READY: Patellofemoral Pain Syndrome (Chondromalacia Patellae).

I have analyzed your presentation: a 23-year-old female with acute onset of worsening knee pain after volleyball (involving repetitive pivoting) and a history advised to lose weight. These factors strongly point to overuse injury and altered biomechanics. The "Pneumonia" diagnosis mentioned in previous records is clinically irrelevant to your knee symptoms. Given the mechanism of injury and patient demographics, the most likely diagnosis is Patellofemoral Pain Syndrome.

To confirm this and rule out other structural issues, could you tell me: Does the pain specifically worsen when you go down stairs, squat, or sit for a long time (theater sign)?
